findings.title: Node.js - Wednesday, November 11, 2026 Security Releases
findings.summary_md: The Node.js project published a consolidated security release for November 11, 2026 covering the 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x lines and 16 vulnerabilities: 7 high, 6 medium, and 3 low severity, most reachable remotely by unauthenticated clients. The flaws concentrate in HTTP/2 and TLS handling, and the advisory lists patched builds v22.23.5, v24.22.3, and v26.13.1 alongside dependency updates to llhttp 9.4.4, undici, and sqlite 3.54.1. Named reporters include Chris Rohlf in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research for CVE-2026-123863, CVE-2026-123864, and CVE-2026-123865, and pimterry for the TLS renegotiation client-certificate bypass CVE-2026-123872. The advisory warns that end-of-life release lines are always affected when a security release occurs.

findings.title: Node.js - Node.js 22.23.5 (LTS)
findings.summary_md: Node.js 22.23.5 (LTS), dated 2026-11-11, is the security release for the 22.x line in the November 2026 batch of 16 vulnerabilities. It carries the C++ HTTP/2 and TLS fixes plus dependency updates to llhttp 9.4.4 and sqlite 3.54.1. The 22.x line is among the lines affected by the HTTPS zero-length TLS write heap read CVE-2026-123864 and the TLS renegotiation client-certificate bypass CVE-2026-123872.

findings.title: Node.js - Node.js 24.22.3 (LTS)
findings.summary_md: Node.js 24.22.3 (LTS), dated 2026-11-11, is the security release for the 24.x line in the November 2026 batch. It carries HTTP/2 and TLS fixes and dependency updates to llhttp 9.4.4, undici, and sqlite 3.54.1. The 24.x line is affected by the remote HTTP/2 abort CVE-2026-123863, the HTTP/2 stream teardown response-memory leak CVE-2026-123866, and the mTLS renegotiation bypass CVE-2026-123872.

findings.title: Node.js - Node.js 26.13.1 (LTS)
findings.summary_md: Node.js 26.13.1, dated 2026-11-11, is the security release for the 26.x line in the November 2026 batch. It carries the same HTTP/2 and TLS fixes and dependency updates to llhttp 9.4.4, undici, and sqlite 3.54.1. The advisory states that on 26.x and 24.x the HTTP/2 stream teardown response-memory leak CVE-2026-123866 can be driven purely by a remote peer once the window-size change from 26.9.0 and 24.22.0 is present.
